name: mutS homolog 2

function.text: MSH2 encodes a DNA mismatch-recognition protein. It forms complexes with MSH6 or MSH3 to recognize mismatched bases and insertion/deletion loops and initiate mismatch repair.

germline.text: Retained constitutional disease associations include Lynch syndrome (autosomal dominant); Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (autosomal recessive). Pathogenicity and inheritance depend on the specific allele and disorder.

somatic.text: Loss of mismatch-repair function involving MSH2 is relevant in colorectal and endometrial carcinomas. Protein-expression loss or an MSI phenotype does not by itself establish a somatic sequence mutation.

function.text: MSH2 encodes a DNA mismatch-recognition protein. It forms part of the post-replicative DNA mismatch repair system (MMR). It forms two different heterodimers: MutS alpha (MSH2-MSH6 heterodimer) and MutS beta (MSH2-MSH3 heterodimer) which binds to DNA mismatches thereby initiating DNA repair. It recruits DNA helicase MCM9 to chromatin which unwinds the mismatch containing DNA strand.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include Lynch syndrome (autosomal dominant); Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: Loss of mismatch-repair function involving MSH2 is relevant in colorectal and endometrial carcinomas.
